subject.title: [Regression]: sessions_spawn missing scope operator.write — introduced between v2026.6.1 and v2026.6.11

question: Should in-process subagent `agent` dispatch use a synthetic `operator.write` client once `sessions_spawn` tool policy has allowed the spawn?
rationale: The bug fix is small, but it intentionally changes which client scopes authorize an internal Gateway write call, so automation should not decide the security boundary alone.

options.title: Confirm Synthetic Write Boundary
options.body: Review and land the linked candidate after real token-auth channel proof if `sessions_spawn` policy is accepted as the authorization boundary.

options.title: Require Broader Gateway Auth Repair
options.body: Pause the linked candidate and design a broader Gateway/device-identity fix that covers this issue and the older auth-scope cluster together.

options.title: Reject That Boundary
options.body: Keep this issue open and ask for an alternative fix that preserves caller-scope inheritance while still restoring channel subagent delegation.

recommendation.title: Confirm Synthetic Write Boundary
recommendation.body: Review and land the linked candidate after real token-auth channel proof if `sessions_spawn` policy is accepted as the authorization boundary.

likelyOwner.reason: They merged the in-process dispatch PR and have recent follow-up history in the affected Gateway dispatch area.
